rationale: The available literature on Popov-Chang syndrome (OMIM #618428) does not substantiate the specific quantitative claim that dysmorphic features (specifically broad forehead, hypertelorism, epicanthus, and depressed nasal bridge) occur in 50-70% of patients. OMIM records dysmorphic facial features qualitatively as present 'in some patients'. Furthermore, FindZebra notes that most individuals have coarse features, frontal bossing, and abnormal eye shape, while the primary discovery paper by Popov et al. (2019) characterizes the YWHAZ-associated presentation as mirroring cardiofaciocutaneous (CFC) syndrome, a RASopathy with distinctive rather than purely nonspecific facial dysmorphisms.

evidence.text: OMIM clinical synopsis notes dysmorphic facial features as occurring qualitatively 'in some patients' rather than providing a 50-70% prevalence or specifying the exact facial features listed.

source.title: 618428 - POPOV-CHANG SYNDROME; POPCHAS
source.quote: Face - Dysmorphic facial features (in some patients)

evidence.text: FindZebra reports that most patients have significant facial dysmorphism, highlighting coarse features, frontal bossing, and abnormal eye shape, rather than the specific combination of broad forehead, epicanthus, and depressed nasal bridge in 50-70%.

source.title: Popov-Chang Syndrome
source.quote: Most patients have significant facial dysmorphism, including coarse features, frontal bossing, and abnormal eye shape. Additional features are highly variable

evidence.text: Popov et al. identified novel YWHAZ variants in individuals presenting with features consistent with cardiofaciocutaneous (CFC) syndrome, which is recognized for a distinctive RASopathy facial gestalt rather than an absence of a recognizable gestalt.

source.title: A YWHAZ Variant Associated With Cardiofaciocutaneous Syndrome
source.quote: Cardiofaciocutaneous (CFC) syndrome is a genetic disorder characterized by distinctive facial features, congenital heart defects, and skin abnormalities... We recently identified novel variants in YWHAZ, a 14-3-3 family member, in individuals with a phenotype consistent with CFC

conflicts: The hypothesis posits that dysmorphic facial features lack a characteristic gestalt and fall into a 50-70% prevalence bracket, whereas primary literature links YWHAZ variants to a cardiofaciocutaneous (CFC)-like phenotype with distinctive craniofacial characteristics.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact frequency of specific HPO craniofacial terms across all clinically published cohorts with pathogenic YWHAZ variants?
new_directions.rationale: Published literature provides qualitative summaries ('some patients', 'most patients') or compares patients to CFC syndrome without systematic numerator/denominator delineations for individual HPO features.

new_directions.question_text: Do computer vision/gestalt recognition tools (e.g., DeepGestalt/Face2Gene) differentiate YWHAZ/Popov-Chang syndrome patients from classical CFC syndrome cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether the dysmorphic features form an identifiable sub-cluster or indistinguishably overlap with classical RASopathy facial gestalts will determine diagnostic discriminating power.
